messages:
alex: Quick triage — seeing model-specific RoPE safety windows collapse after last kernel swap. Need a short bisect and a plan for per-model safe ranges.

maria: Seen it on Llama-2-13B and Mixtral-8x22B. p95 token latency is ok but perplexity on longctx (>8k) drifts up ~2.3 ppl on NTK variant.

jon: Perf numbers from last night run:
```
model: llama-2-13b
kernel: new-opt-v2
batching: adaptive (max 8)
ctx: 12k tokens
ppl: 18.4 -> 20.7 (regressed)
throughput: 430 tok/s -> 420 tok/s
p95 latency: 85ms -> 92ms
```

jon: Mixtral shows bigger hit on NTK RoPE at longctx, but linear RoPE variant looks stable. Qwen seems unaffected.

perf-bot: :warning: Regression alert: rollout new-opt-v2 -> anomaly score 0.72 for llama-2-13b longctx. See /dash/perf/173210.

alex: Thanks — can we confirm whether KV cache indexing or head/kv dimension packing changed? Might be a kernel-level reordering.

maria: Checked KV slot layout: unchanged. But the kernel swapped a fused-attn path that changes the head stride when num_heads % warp_size != 0. That could interact with RoPE interpolation.

sara: Quick attempt: force old kernel on a small pool and run the exact prompt sweep. Command I used:
```
RUNTIME_KERNEL=old-opt
./run_inference_bench --model llama-2-13b --ctx 12000 --batch 4 --prompt-file longctx_sweep.txt
```

jon: Results with old-opt: ppl stable at 18.6, throughput 428 tok/s, p95 88ms. With new-opt-v2 we see ppl 20.7 and occasional perplexity spikes mid-sequence.

maria: Hypothesis: new-opt-v2 applies head-sliced kernel that reorders per-head rotary phase application; small FP rounding error accumulates across longctx for NTK-scaling. Linear RoPE less sensitive.

alex: Can we replicate with a deterministic short test to isolate rotation math? I want minimal IO noise.

jon: Ran a deterministic microtest on cpu/gpu with single prompt (seeded). Diff shows subtle atan2/scale difference at head index boundary 127->128.

maria: That matches: our Mixtral head_kv_dim=128 boundary has a non-power-of-two stride after quantization/packing. New kernel assumes contiguous head packing; it inserts a permute that changes float accumulation order.

perf-bot: Note: quantized kernels may amplify these FP reorder issues. Tracked issue #INF-392.

alex: Two parallel actions: (1) bisect kernel change to exact commit that introduced the permute. (2) short-term mitigation: route affected models (llama-2-13b, mixtral-8x22b) to old-opt kernel for longctx workloads or force linear RoPE variant for NTK-sensitive runs.

sara: I can add a routing rule in runtime policy:
```
match: model in ["llama-2-13b","mixtral-8x22b"] and ctx >= 8k
action: kernel=old-opt
```
I'll stage in canary cluster.

jon: Bisect update: commit 7f3b2d swapped fused-attn ordering. Repro at that commit. Adding a minimal patch to preserve head accumulation order fixes ppl in our microtest.

maria: Patch looks good. But we should also compute per-model safe RoPE ranges: e.g., for llama-2-13b NTK we recommend ctx<=8192 or use linear variant. Mixtral safe range slightly higher with patched kernel. Qwen unaffected.

alex: Good. Let's also add a regression eval to Redwood Optimize that runs these longctx prompts nightly across kernel variants. Add an alert if ppl delta > 1.0 vs baseline.

perf-bot: Added nightly job: longctx-rope-eval -> job id 173210-nightly. Threshold set to 1.0 ppl.

infra-bot: Deployed runtime route canary to 10% traffic. Old-opt routing for matching models enabled.

sara: Can we avoid routing churn for dedicated customers? Prefer a config knob: `rope_safety_mode: auto|legacy|force_linear`. I'll draft a PR.

alex: Please do. Include observability to show per-route ppl and token-level diffs. Also annotate model catalog with safe ranges and recommended RoPE variant.

maria: I'll update model catalog table: add fields `rope_variant_safe_ranges` and `kernel_compat`. Example entry: 
```
llama-2-13b: {ntk_safe: 0-8192, linear_safe: 0-16384, kernel_compat: old-opt}
```

jon: Final note — we should audit other kernels for similar head-packing assumptions. I'll add a perf task to run head/kv-dim boundary tests (64/128/192/256).

alex: Great. Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: jon -> bisect PR + boundary tests, sara -> runtime route PR, maria -> model catalog update, infra -> canary monitor. Reopen if regressions persist. :thumbsup:
